question.leadin: The Cavalier poets were so called because they supported this leader in the English Civil War.
question.text: Name this son of James I, who was disliked by his country's legislature. He was executed after the English Civil War.
question.clue: This ruler was depicted "at the hunt" by his court painter, Anthony van Dyck.

swap.text: The Magna Carta was signed by this king, the youngest of five sons of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine.
swap.clue: He allegedly murdered his nephew Arthur of Brittany and at the Battle of Mirabeau he rescued his mother Eleanor of Aquitaine.

question.text: This first ruler from the House of Normandy ruled from 1066-1087 following his victory at the Battle of Hastings.
question.answerHtml: William I [accept William the Conqueror or William the Bastard; prompt on “William”]
question.clue: An Archbishop of Canterbury named Stigand stands next to this ruler in one depiction commissioned by his half-brother Odo.

swap.text: At the end of the War of Spanish Secession, Britain gained this overseas possession on the Southern coast of Spain. Its namesake Rock is one of the Pillars of Hercules.
swap.clue: During the American Revolution, this place was invested in a three year and seven month "great siege" by France and Spain.

question.leadin: This country is one of the few that still has a Historiographer Royal.
question.text: Name this European country, whose Neolithic archaeological sites include Skara Brae ("SKAR-ah BRAY") on the Orkney Islands.
question.clue: Peter and Eileen Caddy founded the New Age Findhorn Community in this country.

swap.leadin: Sir William Stanley's reinforcements turned the tide of this battle.
swap.text: Name this 1485 battle, during which forces under the future Henry VII defeated Richard III.
swap.clue: The leader of the losing army managed to unhorse John Cheyne and kill Sir William Brandon, but failed to receive assistance from Henry Percy's reserves.

question.leadin: A legend claims that while this king was on the run, he took refuge in a peasant woman's house but let her cakes burn under his watch to the woman's great displeasure.
question.text: Name this early Anglo-Saxon king of Wessex whose rule was chronicled by the bishop Asser. This king translated Boethius' Consolation of Philosophy and fought against the Viking leader Guthrum.
question.clue: He is traditionally credited with founding the English navy.

swap.leadin: Societies of these people included free peasant laborers called churls and adapted an elite warrior class called huscarls from Viking raiders, who they had to pay in danegeld.
swap.text: Name these Germanic people who joined the Jutes in settling lower Britain between the rule of the Romans and the conquest of the Normans.
swap.answerHtml: Anglo-Saxons [or the Angles and Saxons; prompt “English” or “England”]
swap.clue: These people were protected by forts called burhs during the Heptarchy.

question.leadin: Answer these questions on the Duke of Suffolk.
question.text: William de la Pole, the duke of Suffolk, sided with this king during the Wars of the Roses.
question.clue: This king was deposed and fled to Scotland following the Battle of Towton.

swap.leadin: Lord Sidmouth's repressive Six Acts were passed in the aftermath of this event.
swap.text: Name this event in which William Hulton's 15th Hussars cavalry charged upon a crowd of reformers in Manchester.
swap.clue: Public meetings concerning church or state were banned by legislation following this event, which sparked unrest along with the earlier Spa Fields Riots.

question.text: This British poet gave an impassioned speech against the frame-breaking law in the House of Lords; you know him better for the fame he was experiencing at the time for his "Childe Harold's Pilgrimage."

swap.leadin: This politician intervened in the Ford machinists' strike of 1968 and published the white paper In Place of Strife while serving as Employment Secretary in 1969.
swap.text: Name this MP for Blackburn who served as both Secretary of State for Health and Minister for Transport in the 1960s and 1970s. This woman was frozen out when her rival James Callaghan became Prime Minister.
swap.clue: Following a protracted series of on-and-off strikes throughout the 1960s, this Secretary of State for Employment and Productivity proposed a White Paper called In Place of Strife in 1969, which imposed requirements that had to be met before a strike was called.

question.text: During the Cadiz Expedition, a general with this surname allowed his men to drink captured wine, leading to his drunk army's easy capture. During his time as Lord High Treasurer, an advisor with this surname may have convinced Queen Elizabeth I to execute Mary, Queen of Scots.
question.clue: The Polish princess Catherine Radziwill, who falsely claimed to be engaged to this man, wrote a posthumous biography of him subtitled "man and empire-maker."

swap.leadin: This man was made Baron of Rievaulx upon his resignation as Prime Minister.
swap.text: Name this man who was succeeded as UK Prime Minister by James Callaghan.
swap.clue: This Labour PM served nonconsecutive terms in the 1960s and 70s. He avoided the Vietnam War and opposed Enoch Powell's "Rivers of Blood speech."

question.leadin: Description acceptable. Stale sandwiches provided by one service were a common talking point supporting this policy, which led to the creation of companies like Connex.
question.text: Identify or describe this policy in John Major's 1992 platform, which critics claim reduced safety standards and led to accidents at Southall, Ladbroke Grove, and Hatfield.
question.answerHtml: privatization of British Rail [accept answers involving turning over public rail infrastructure to private owners or companies]

swap.text: The Urbinese diplomat Polydore Vergil claimed that Wolsey had "thrust" this older Archbishop of Canterbury aside when Wolsey succeeded him as Lord Chancellor in 1515.

question.text: This 1942 document outlined the plan for a British welfare state that would fix the "five great evils" of "want, disease, ignorance, squalor and idleness".
question.clue: This document identified squalor, ignorance, want, idleness, and disease as the "Five Giant Evils" plaguing society.

swap.leadin: Its captain was the son of the man who served as captain of the Mora, the ship William the Conqueror used in his invasion of England.
swap.text: Name this vessel that met its demise on a return trip from Normandy to England in November of 1120 CE. It's believed that the captain tried to race the English king's ship back to England when he struck a rock.
swap.clue: The succession crisis following Henry I was caused by the death of the king's only heir aboard this ship. Henry of Huntingdon claimed that it sank as a judgement from heaven due to the number of sodomites on it.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about a European custom, FTP each.
question.text: According to this rule inheritance preference was granted to daughters of a first marriage over sons of subsequent marriages. Louis XIV attempted to invoke it to gain the Spanish Netherlands in starting a namesake war in 1667.
question.clue: This procedure, which occurred for Wales in 1997, leading to the creation of the Senedd ("SEN-eth").

swap.text: Sands was held in this prison during his hunger strike, during which he was elected to parliament as a member of its anti-H block group. Liam Averill escaped from here by dressing up as a woman during a Christmas party.
